assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new observational window: a cubic-kilometre Cherenkov detector in Antarctic ice that detected astrophysical neutrinos (2013), later associated with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane. This is a detector-driven discovery of the kind I value most, joining particle physics and astronomy and opening neutrino astronomy.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit names only Halzen, who conceived and led IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA and drove the science case. A fair prize would likely need to recognise the collaboration's instrument builders, but the credited string supports only one laureate. I cannot independently verify the full division of credit among IceCube leaders.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is good: the diffuse flux has been measured with several channels and, from 2023 on, Galactic-plane emission. Source identification is only partly established (a few sources, with NGC 1068 as another), so the astrophysics is still maturing, but the discovery of cosmic neutrinos is solid and timely.
uncertainties: Allocation: a single credited name may not reflect who built and led the instrument.
Source associations beyond TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 are still at moderate significance.
I rely on memory for the details of the IceCube milestones.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The localisation of gamma-ray bursts by BeppoSAX and the optical and radio afterglows that followed settled the cosmological origin of GRBs, one of the major puzzles of high-energy astrophysics. It rests on a clear instrumental step: arcminute X-ray localisation fast enough for follow-up.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX Wide Field Cameras and Gamma-Ray Burst Monitor, which gave the localisation. Kulkarni's group delivered the optical, radio and redshift follow-up. This is a natural experiment-plus-follow-up split. Other people (e.g. van Paradijs, Groot, Djorgovski, Metzger) are not in the credited names, and I cannot say whether the omission is a fair concern.
assessment.maturity: Nearly 30 years of confirmation: thousands of afterglows, redshifts, GRB-supernova links and connections to neutron-star mergers. The interpretation has been stable, and recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit beyond the three credited names (for example the optical discovery team) may be disputed.
Whether the committee sees this as physics or astronomy is for colleagues to judge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reached uncertainties near 10^-18, a roughly hundredfold gain over the caesium standard. They enable tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a redefinition of the second. A precision-measurement achievement with clear technique, calibration and systematics work behind it.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice and made the first demonstration. Ye's group pushed it to the 10^-18 level and developed strontium clock systematics and the frequency-comb link. The two-name configuration is clean, although Hall and Hänsch (2005) and Wineland (2012) already sit nearby in the prize history, and the lattice-clock priority may be contested by others (e.g. Lemonde, Gill, Ludlow).
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, NIST, PTB, SYRTE) have confirmed 10^-18 performance, and the technique is stable. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier clock-related prizes may weigh against it.
Other groups' contributions to the lattice clock are outside the credited names.
I am not an AMO expert and defer to colleagues on the history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The conception and construction of ATLAS and CMS made the 2012 observation of the Higgs boson possible. These are among the most demanding detectors ever built. I know the field from the inside. The 2013 prize recognised the theory, not the experimental discovery.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are the founding spokespersons and leading architects of ATLAS and CMS. This is a plausible three-person configuration, but it recognises detector leadership in preference to individual analysts, and the statutes limit three laureates for a collaboration of thousands. Some committee colleagues may worry about how the discovery itself is credited.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the Higgs boson has been independently seen in two experiments and its couplings measured over more than a decade. Timing is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wishes to honour experimental leadership after the 2013 theory prize.
The role of other founders, such as the early LHC and accelerator leadership, is not covered by the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical flat-band prediction at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene launched the field of moiré quantum matter, with a large and rapid impact across condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald 2011 continuum model predicted the magic angle. Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experiments with Cao et al. The credited trio is an acceptable theory-plus-experiment split, though Cao as lead author and Dean/Kim groups' parallel work are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have reproduced the correlated phases and the field has expanded into fractional Chern insulators and beyond. The origin of the superconductivity is still debated, and I rely on colleagues in condensed matter to judge it.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism remains open.
Credit given to graduate students and other groups is not captured in the credited names.
This is outside my own field and my confidence is lower.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices turned quantum many-body models (the Mott transition, Hubbard physics) into controllable laboratory systems, with single-site imaging in quantum gas microscopes. The technique has changed how many-body physics is tested.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch-Zoller proposal, followed by Greiner and Bloch's Mott insulator experiment, and Esslinger's fermionic Hubbard work are central. The credited list holds five names, so any prize needs a choice. I propose the three leading experimentalists, which leaves out the theorists Cirac and Zoller and may be contentious.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across many labs for two decades. Some Nobel recognition for ultracold atoms already exists (2001, 1997), so the novelty relative to past prizes needs discussion.
uncertainties: Theory-versus-experiment allocation is unresolved.
Overlap with earlier ultracold-atom prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry uses matter-wave interference for gravimetry, tests of the equivalence principle and measurement of constants. As an instrument-builder I value the sensors, with practical applications in navigation and geodesy.
assessment.attribution: Bordé, Pritchard and Kasevich-Chu developed the key light-pulse interferometers in the 1980s-90s. Schmiedmayer's contributions (chip and BEC interferometry) are strong but I leave him out of this three-person proposal. The allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Technique is mature and widely used, and applications in precision gravimetry are real. Fundamental physics results are still limited, but the instrument is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Which three of four credited people have the decisive claim is unclear.
Overlap with the 1997 and 2001 AMO prizes.
I rely on colleagues for the AMO history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Ti:sapphire laser and the mode-locking methods (Kerr-lens, SESAM) gave the compact femtosecond source that underlies attosecond physics (the 2023 prize), frequency combs and ultrafast spectroscopy. It is a durable enabling instrument.
assessment.attribution: Moulton invented the Ti:sapphire gain medium, Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode-locking, and Keller invented the SESAM. This is a plausible three-person split, although others (e.g. Spence, Kapteyn, Murnane) may also have claims.
assessment.maturity: Mature and decades old with universal adoption. Recognition is late rather than premature, but recent prizes (2018, 2023) near this area may reduce its priority.
uncertainties: Priority disputes around Kerr-lens mode-locking.
Proximity to the 2018 and 2023 prizes.
